subject.title: Gateway drops concurrent in-process tool-to-gateway WebSocket connections (1006) under parallel tool fan-out; misleading Gateway-crashed error (2026.6.11)

question: Should agent-originated platform tools keep per-call Gateway WebSocket RPC with throttling, move to a shared/in-process Gateway dispatch path, or be folded into the broader Gateway event-loop pressure plan?
rationale: The choice crosses Gateway auth/scopes, plugin/tool ownership, transport semantics, and scheduler policy, so a code worker should not pick the permanent architecture from the issue alone.

options.title: Throttle current RPC path
options.body: Keep the existing Gateway RPC boundary, add bounded per-turn or per-tool concurrency for agent-originated platform calls, and improve 1006 diagnostics as the first repair.

options.title: Design in-process dispatch
options.body: Create a trusted in-process Gateway method dispatch path for embedded-agent platform tools, which may remove loopback self-connections but needs careful auth and plugin-boundary review.

options.title: Fold into broad pressure tracker
options.body: Treat this as a symptom of https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/78861 and only preserve the specific cron fan-out/error-text evidence there.

recommendation.title: Throttle current RPC path
recommendation.body: Keep the existing Gateway RPC boundary, add bounded per-turn or per-tool concurrency for agent-originated platform calls, and improve 1006 diagnostics as the first repair.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the clearest sampled ownership of the Gateway control plane and is the best available routing owner for choosing the RPC boundary.
